## Runtime parts (src/, take effect only when R81 is installed)
- **`src/repair/ci-first-policy.ts`:** `HOSTED_PRE_REVIEW_CI_FIXES = true`. In a hosted run, the gate now gives a red head with no completed review the CI fix marker instead of a park. That covers new candidates and reviewed records' refreshed heads.
  - The matrix planner then plans a fix cell charged in `counters.retries`. It never counts as a review round, there are at most 3 per record, and after that the record gets the exhausted park.
  - No new state shape, cell kind or stdout line.
- **`src/repair/loop-ci-first.ts`, `src/host/matrix-planner.ts`:** comment changes only.
- I checked that no launcher code path reads this flag. The ops/ graph imports only matrix ingest and `settleFailedImplementation`, so flipping it does not change launcher behaviour.

## Launcher-only parts (ops/, may ship before the runtime, correct under R80)
- **`planCiFirstReadmission` (`ops/hosted-autonomy-retries.ts`), moved base:** under a proven CI-first runtime (R80 included), a red or pending pre-review park whose base moved goes back to `work`. It is uncharged, gets no marker, and logs `...:base-moved`.
  - The runtime's freshness gate refreshes it deterministically, then gates CI before any review.
  - It requires a review round left (`reviewRoundsLeft > 0`). Otherwise the runtime's ceiling gate would park it before the refresh. A legacy record whose final round is not yet armed is left to the fix rule instead.
  - The refresh takes precedence over the fix rule.
  - The unchanged-base condition now applies only to the any-runtime green rule.
- **Exhausted park (`preReviewCiExhausted` / `preReviewGateParked`):** it now gets the once-per-head re-run and the green rule, never a fix or a moved-base refresh. This applies only when no completed review binds the head.
  - The merge gate (`loop-ci-correction.ts:161`) writes the same message for reviewed heads. Returning those to `work` would buy a needless extra review round, so they keep generation 80's behaviour.
- **Ready to pin R81:**
  - `HOSTED_AUTONOMY_CI_FIRST_FIX_RUNTIMES` stays empty.
  - New `HOSTED_AUTONOMY_CI_FIRST_FIX_MIN_GENERATION = 81` and `ciFirstFixRuntimeProven`, which requires generation 81 or later, the CI-first allowlist, and the runtime's own healthy proof. The planner and retry pass use it.
  - New tests check that the fix allowlist is a subset of the CI-first and CI-correction allowlists, and that every listed revision present locally has the flag set to true in its own tree.
- **Test comment fixed:** `tests/host/hosted-autonomy-ci-first_test.ts:177`.
- **`docs/DECISIONS.md`:** new "Generation 81 pre-review CI fixes" section, and the generation-80 wording about the exhausted park is updated.

- **Matrix cell check:** R80's matrix consumer (`matrix-artifact-wave.ts`, unchanged from R80) isolates the pre-review fix cell as a runtime mismatch with the charge kept reserved. It does this for a never-reviewed head, for a reviewed record's refreshed head, and for both legacy shapes. The two shapes no planner grants (uncharged fix, other base) still get the generic refusal. So R80 refuses nothing it already handled.
- **Parsers:** R80's parsers accept the hosted planner's real plan and every snapshot that the gate, planner and retry pass write.
- **R80's own loop:**
  - It parks the CI fix marker precisely (`CI red before review…`) and uncharged.

findings.summary: The moved-base return has no per-pass cap. Under R80, where the fix route is closed, a candidate-caused red park is refreshed and parked again once per base move until R81 is pinned.
findings.failure_scenario: 18 parks today, and ai.ubq.fi development moves 16 to 25 times a day. Each pass hands the runtime every moved park, uncharged. Under R80 each refresh pushes a new head and runs CI. A red result parks again, and the next base move repeats the cycle. That is up to several hundred refresh pushes and CI runs a day until R81 is pinned as a fix runtime. Nothing unsafe follows: no review round or fix is charged and nothing red is reviewed or merged. The cost is CI time and PR churn.
findings.suggested_fix: Optionally bound the moved-base returns per pass, for example with a dedicated rotating cap like HOSTED_AUTONOMY_SPENT_CI_READS_PER_PASS. Alternatively, keep the behaviour and schedule the R81 fix-runtime pin promptly after R81 is healthy.

findings.summary: rerunShape now covers the exhausted park, but it does not check that a review round is left, so a head the green rule would refuse can still use its one re-run.
findings.failure_scenario: An exhausted pre-review park with no round left (reviewRoundsLeft = 0, e.g. reviewRounds 3) on its unchanged, green base gets its failed run re-run in the delivery pass. Next pass the green read succeeds, but planCiFirstReadmission requires roundLeft, so nothing is re-admitted. One CI re-run is wasted. The same pre-existing gap applies to red parks with no round.
findings.suggested_fix: Add reviewRoundAvailable(snapshot, record, cutoff) to the pre-review arm of rerunShape. Alternatively, leave it and document the wasted re-run.

findings.summary: The merge gate's exhausted park of a reviewed head still gets neither a flake re-run nor a green re-delivery. This is out of #153's scope, so it is a follow-up.
findings.failure_scenario: A reviewed head whose 3 CI fixes are spent is parked by loop-ci-correction.ts:161 with 'CI fix attempts exhausted (3 of 3)'. If its last red was a flake, the head turns green on its unchanged reviewed base and stays parked forever. GREEN_PREFIXES in ops/hosted-autonomy-ci-retries.ts excludes that message, and preReviewCiExhausted excludes reviewed heads. Correctly, the lane does not send it to work, which would cost a review round. But returning it to delivery would need no review round.
findings.suggested_fix: Follow-up issue: let the once-per-head re-run and the green rule return a merge-gate exhausted park to `delivery` (not `work`) on its exact reviewed base.

Lane #154 is in place: required CI now counts as green only when every expected check exists, in the runtime gates and the launcher. The suite does not run fully clean here. The failures that remain also fail on unchanged L80 in this environment, and one file times out at 300s on L80 too (details at the end).

**I did not use the base's raw check names.** Live sentinel `development` 9a1b1d924 holds `dispatch` (a run every five minutes from the schedule) beside `test-local`, and no PR head ever runs `dispatch`. Requiring the base's raw names would hold every self head forever. The rule instead (`missingExpectedChecks`, new file src/repair/ci-coverage.ts) is: the head must report every check name of each base check suite that shares at least one name with it. Base suites the head shares nothing with, and commit statuses, are never required. ai.ubq.fi (only `deno-deploy.yml` on development, four jobs, one suite) is covered fully.

**Runtime parts (take effect when generation 81 installs; src/):**
- `GitHubCheckV1.suite` is now read from `check_suite.id` in src/github/wire.ts. It is not persisted, and a malformed value fails the parse.
- `absentExpectedChecks` in loop-checks.ts reads the base and returns the missing names, or null when the base read fails.
- **CI-first gate** (`gateReviewOnCi`): a green head is reviewed only once it covers `record.target.base`. Until then it gets the existing `ci_pending` wait (uncharged, `since` kept). After 6h it parks as `CI did not finish before review within 6 hours: verify-artifact(absent)`. An unreadable base read defers.
- **`spentOnMovedBase`**: a spent reviewed head is refreshed only after it covers its reviewed base. It waits at `delivery` and parks under `REVIEW_ROUND_CEILING_REVIEWED_CI_PENDING_PREFIX`.
- **`executeCarriedDelivery`**: the carried-merge marker is written only after H1 covers T. It parks under `REVIEW_ROUND_CEILING_CARRIED_CI_PENDING_PREFIX`.
- **Unchanged:** `gateDeliveryOnChecks` (the runtime's merge, release and closure gates) and the self merge ports. Those heads already passed the CI-first gate, self CI is the single `test-local` job, and the runtime's port refuses ai.ubq.fi merges.

**Launcher-only parts (ops/; can ship before the runtime — they import only the pure rule file):**
- `hasAllChecksGreen(head, base?)` now returns `true | false | null`. Null means the listing (head or base) was unreadable, incomplete, malformed, or the head has no check runs.
- `headIsGreen` now passes the base. `preMergeGate` uses the reviewed base and `carriedMergeGate` uses T, so a marker that R80 writes during the gap merges nothing (`checks_pending`).
- **Retry pass:** foreign heads are read against their record base. A head enters `ciReadHeads` only after a successful non-empty listing. Unreadable heads go into a new `ciUnreadHeads` and get no CI correction or CI fix plan, whether or not their review rounds are spent.
- `hosted-autonomy-ci-rerun.ts` and the closure gate use `=== true`.
- These reads keep the head-only rule: the tip's own CI, the closure gate, and lost-write adoption.

**R80 rollback:** every write is a shape R80 already writes (`ci_pending` waits and parks under the existing prefixes). I added `gen80Available`, `loadGen80Modules` (which also extracts R80's `ops/`), `loadGen80Parsers` and `assertGen80Parses` beside the gen-79 helpers, guarded so they skip when R80's source is absent. The new tests parse every write under R80 and run R80's own `preReviewCiParked` on the new park message (true). docs/DECISIONS.md has a new section, "Required CI coverage (issue #154, generation 81)".

findings.summary: The new coverage read `absentExpectedChecks` uses the strict runtime `readChecks(base)`. That read rejects every live sentinel `development` tip, so every self (ubiquity/sentinel) head is deferred forever: never reviewed, never refreshed, never carried, and never given a wait or a park. The same null-to-defer happens at loop-ci-first.ts:242 and loop-carried-delivery.ts:241 and :490.
findings.failure_scenario: sentinel-supervisor is fast-forwarded together with development, so supervisor.yml runs on the dev tip SHA and adds `matrix_cell (<64-hex cellId>)` check runs. Those names are 78 characters long. Live counts: 3f041b46d (the current tip) has 69 runs, 32 of them matrix_cell; 9a1b1d924 has 7; 01f482529 has 6. parseCheckRunWire bounds the name at MaxText.label = 64 (wire.ts:316), so `readChecks(base)` returns `unavailable: GitHub API response exceeds contract bounds`. Then `absentExpectedChecks` returns null and `gateReviewOnCi` returns UNAVAILABLE: a deferral with no write, no `ci_pending` wait, no 6-hour bound and no park, so no launcher rule can re-admit the record. Live self records issue-ubiquity-sentinel-152, -155 and -156 sit on base 3f041b46d. Once R81 is installed, any green `test-local` head they publish stalls silently at the review gate. Repro at HEAD 394b524b, through the real GitHubPortImpl over the live 9a1b1d924 listing: scratchpad/gen81-review2-154/evidence/zz_review154_test.ts ran 3 runs 7 hours apart and ended at nextStep=work, wait=null, blocker=null, with no requestReview. The spent moved-base step behaves the same: evidence/zz_carried_probe_test.ts ran 4 runs 7 hours apart and ended with refreshes=0, step=delivery, wait=null, blocker=null. `executeCarriedDelivery` makes the same T read, so a carried self H1 never gets its marker. A stalled self record at base == tip is also returned by `deliveryQueueAhead`, so other self records on a moved base wait behind it (`... goes first`). The lane's own self test uses synthetic short names. Its report claims 'a self head is not held', but that only holds for those synthetic names. The uncommitted live-self test edits in the lane worktree fail at HEAD with 'work' !== 'review'.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the coverage rule in the runtime only where it is needed. Skip it for the self repository, as the launcher already does: the self gate is the single named `test-local` job and its base suites never share a name with a PR head beyond that. Alternatively, give coverage its own lenient base read that takes only name and check_suite.id, applies no 64-character label bound, and keeps an item bound. A name longer than 64 characters cannot be on a strictly read head anyway. An unreadable base read should also become a bounded `ci_pending` wait or park, never an unbounded silent deferral. Add regression tests through the real port over the live 3f041b46d / 9a1b1d924 listings for the CI-first gate, `spentOnMovedBase` and `executeCarriedDelivery`. The same root cause already exists, out of this lane's scope, in the red-path base read at loop-ci-first.ts:263, which R80 also has.

findings.summary: The accepted residual is stated wrongly. It says a base read inside the base's own gap needs 'both five-second windows to overlap'. In fact the base lacks its `needs:` job for its whole first stage, not for five seconds.
findings.failure_scenario: T has no `verify-artifact` check run from the start of its push run until validate, mac-containment and darwin-native finish, about 20 minutes on ai.ubq.fi. A carried H1 refreshed onto a just-merged T therefore escapes the rule whenever T's first stage is still running when H1 reaches its 5-second gap. That happens with a fast refresh, or when T's runners queue longer. Then neither the runtime marker step nor the launcher's carriedMergeGate expects verify-artifact, and H1 merges with its required job never run. In the live PR 1064 case T was 14.5 minutes ahead, so that case is covered, but the residual is wider than documented.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat a shared base suite that is not complete (any run in it not yet `completed`) as an incomplete expectation and wait, bounded. Or, in the launcher's preMergeGate and carriedMergeGate, also require every head workflow run (`listHeadRuns`, already read in carriedMergeGate) to be completed. Fix the DECISIONS wording.

findings.summary: A base suite counts as expected when it shares any single check name with the head. A different workflow on the base that happens to reuse a generic job name (`build`, `test`, `lint`) makes all of its jobs required on every head.
findings.failure_scenario: Suppose a target adds a push-only workflow on development with jobs `test` and `deploy`, while its PR workflow also has a `test` job. Every head then lacks `deploy`. It waits 6 hours, then parks. The REVIEWED_CI_PENDING and CARRIED_CI_PENDING parks are final for spent and carried records, and the launcher's preMergeGate refuses `checks_pending` forever. Not live today: ai.ubq.fi has one workflow, and sentinel's job names are disjoint from `test-local`.
findings.suggested_fix: Match base suites to head suites by workflow identity (for example `check_suite.app` plus the workflow path from the workflow-run listing) rather than by any shared name. Or record this as an explicit residual with the job-name constraint.

Worktree: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/c10997af-52cc-5780-962c-3522871e2f8f/scratchpad/wt81-154. Its tree is clean. Nothing was pushed, dispatched or posted, and no live state was written.

**Prior attempt:** the uncommitted live-self test edits from the interrupted run were kept and reworked. At 394b524b they failed as the finding said (`'work' !== 'review'`, `refreshes 0 !== 1`).

**Disposition: P1 src/repair/loop-checks.ts:65, fixed.** Everything in this amendment is runtime code under `src/`. Nothing under `ops/` changed, so the lane's launcher parts can still ship before the runtime.
- **Self scope skips the base read.** `absentExpectedChecks(deps, record, head)` returns `[]` for ubiquity/sentinel at installation 0 without reading the base, as the launcher already does. The self gate is the single `test-local` job.
- **New lenient coverage read for every other repository.** `GitHubPort.readCheckSuites(sha)` returns only each check run's name and `check_suite.id`. It has no 64-character label bound, keeps the exact-head and item bounds, and skips commit statuses. It is implemented in `client-reads.ts` (shares the check-run collection with `readChecks`) and `port-base.ts`, with `parseCheckSuiteMemberWire` in `wire.ts`.
- **Strict read reverted.** `readChecks` and `parseCheckRunWire` are exactly R80's again, and `GitHubCheckV1.suite` is gone. A malformed suite on a head can no longer make the head unreadable.
- **Unreadable base now waits and parks.** At loop-ci-first.ts and both sites in loop-carried-delivery.ts (`spentOnMovedBase`, `executeCarriedDelivery`), an unreadable base becomes the existing bounded `ci_pending` wait. After the bound it parks under the existing prefix with `base checks unreadable` (`absentCheckLabels(null)`). Every write is an R80 shape.
- **Not changed (out of scope):** an unreadable head read still defers, as in R80. The red-path strict base read at loop-ci-first.ts:263 is R80's own. Both are recorded in docs/DECISIONS.md, along with a new accepted residual: a self workflow that gains a `needs:` job is not covered.

**Tests** (each one new or changed below failed against the pre-fix runtime and passes now):
- New fixture: tests/fixtures/repair/sentinel-development-check-runs-live.json, read-only snapshots taken at 23:17Z. It holds 9a1b1d924 (22 runs, 7 over 64 characters) and 3f041b46d (75 runs, 33 over 64 characters).
- **CI-first gate**, through the real `GitHubPortImpl` on both listings: a self head is reviewed without reading the base; a foreign head is reviewed through `readCheckSuites`, which requests check-runs only. An unreadable base waits, parks after 6 hours, is parsed by R80, and R80's `preReviewCiParked` accepts the park.
- **Carried path**, through the real port with B0 on the L80 listing and T on the current tip, self and foreign: `spentOnMovedBase` refreshes the head and `executeCarriedDelivery` writes the marker. Unreadable B0 or T waits and then parks under the REVIEWED / CARRIED CI_PENDING prefixes.
- **Port tests:** strict-versus-lenient reads of the live listings, plus head-drift, malformed-suite, empty-name and item-bound refusals.
- **Gates:**
  - `deno fmt --check`, `deno lint`, `ops/code-size.ts check` and the test-local `deno check` list all pass.
  - The full `tests/` tree ran in 101 batches of at most 4 files. Three batches hit the 300-second limit; their files pass one at a time (candidate-handoff-cuts split into its two tests).
  - The four coverage files pass (31 tests) in a shallow clone without the R80 source, so the R80 guards hold.
- **Failures not caused by this change:** these also fail on a clean 9a1b1d924 checkout here, on the same tests apart from timing flakes in replay/runtime_test. They come from this container: the worktree sits under /tmp, which `--allow-write=/tmp` covers, and the bwrap/process-group sandbox and trusted binary paths differ from CI.
